overall_reason: The page shows no label that it is a specimen (only its URL path suggests one), so I judge it as a ship landing page in Persuade mode; the decisive claim is 'Trusted by 10,000+ forward-thinking teams worldwide' over six unlinked default-cast wordmarks (Northwind, Halcyon, Meridian, Fieldnote, Atlas & Co., Verity); the sweep's INT-001 and INT-002 hits on them stand.

score.reason: T-PROOF-SOURCE fails on the 'Trusted by 10,000+' row (INT-010, Floor, with the sweep's INT-001 and INT-002 hits) and on the SOC 2 claim (INT-022), and T-PROMISE-LINK finds dead 'Customers' and 'Pricing' links (INT-016).

findings.where: hero 'Trusted by' line and the logo row under it (section.logos), first screen, 1440 and 375; tiles/1440-00.png and tiles/1440-01.png
findings.evidence: The first screen ends with 'Trusted by 10,000+ forward-thinking teams worldwide', which the sweep fails (invented_metrics, INT-001, social-proof-counts). The row under it lists six unlinked wordmarks: 'Northwind', 'Halcyon', 'Meridian', 'Fieldnote', 'Atlas & Co.', 'Verity' (claims table logo wall, linked 0), and the sweep's default_names check fails Northwind, Halcyon and Fieldnote (INT-002). No case study, quote or link stands behind any name, and the closing line repeats the claim as 'Join thousands of teams'.
findings.before: "Trusted by 10,000+ forward-thinking teams worldwide" over Northwind, Halcyon, Meridian, Fieldnote, Atlas & Co., Verity
findings.after: Remove the line and the row together, or use real customers' marks with permission and a dated, sourced count: [DATA NEEDED: real customers and count].
findings.why: The row is the page's only proof, and every name in it comes from the default cast; a visitor who searches one finds nothing.

findings.evidence: The card says 'SOC 2 compliant infrastructure with end-to-end encryption. Your data is safe, always.' Nothing on the page backs it: no report, no auditor, no trust page, and the 'Docs' link is '#'.
findings.before: "SOC 2 compliant infrastructure ... Your data is safe, always."
findings.after: State SOC 2 only if the client holds a report, and link it; otherwise describe the actual security measures.
findings.why: A compliance claim with nothing behind it is a label of standing the visitor cannot check.

findings.evidence: The claims table counts 10 dead links (href '#'), among them 'Product', 'Solutions', 'Pricing', 'Customers' and 'Docs'. 'Customers' should hold the evidence for '10,000+ teams', and 'Pricing' should hold the terms of the 'Start free trial' offer.
findings.after: Link real customers and pricing pages, or remove the links with the claims they support.
findings.why: The links promise proof and terms and go nowhere, so the visitor cannot check the trial or the customers.
